technical_complexity.rationale: Inserting ads inside streaming video needs a video player integration and ad serving; sources give no detail of what Vapor built.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of data, contracts or technology lock-in was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YouTube already ran in-video overlay ads in 2007 (Fortune, 2007-08-24); no source describes what incumbents did about Vapor.

market_need_then: Streaming Media's 2011 state of online video advertising and an estimated $4.3 billion US online video ad market by 2011 (eMarketer, via a 2009 Innovid article) show spend, but nothing Vapor specific.

branding.domain_note: YC lists askolo.com, which did not resolve when fetched, so no source ties the Vapor name to a domain.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding searches returned only unrelated vaping companies and a 2025 ad-fraud operation also named Vapor; nothing on this company's brand.

outcome_analysis: Vapor was a YC S11 in-video advertising startup from four listed founders. The only funding figure is an undated $125K on Dealroom, and no coverage, traction or shutdown notice was found, so the cause of the end is not public. The generic name overlaps with later unrelated Vapor brands but no source shows it hurt the company; the brand_confusion factor is a weak judgment and the cause of failure remains unknown.
notes: The YC page currently describes modular server side software with Swift, which looks like text from a different Vapor project, and lists askolo.com as the site (DNS failed, possibly outside the session's allowed domains). The Dealroom $125K figure came from a search summary; the Dealroom page itself returned HTTP 429 and was not opened, and it rests on one database. Round Funded labels the company acquired on an ambiguous layout; not used. Prior employers other than a later Microsoft sale are not recorded. Competitor sources are dated February 2011 and 2008; Innovid is older than the batch.
